1 This case is arising out of charge sheet filed by PSI of K.R. Puram Tr Police in Cr. No. 147/2019 against accused No.1 & 2 for the alleged offence p/u/s. 279, 337 & 304(A) IPC & 134(A&B) r/w 187 IMV Act.
2.
The brief facts of the prosecution case are as follows:

On 26.06.2019, at about morning 3:00 am accused No.1 Veerappa, being driver of JBC bearing No. KA-53 N 5264 drove his vehicle, at Mahadevpura Ring Road, Service Road, on the left side of the road, near Kebab Magic Hotel.
He was digging the road to lay electric cables without giving any signal.
He rashly and negligently turned the bucket of the JCB to the right side.

As a result of turning the bucket to the right, JCB dashed to the motorcycle bearing No. KA 04 JU 6918 which was coming from from K.
R. Pura railway station towards Marathalli, i.e., from north to south direction.
Due to the accident, the motorcycle rider and the pillion rider fell down on the road.

The rider Yashwanth.K sustained simple injuries and the pillion rider Ramesh. K.P.
sustained grievous blood injuries on his head, ears and nose and mouth and he succumbed to the occurrence in the Jeevika Hospital.

Accused No.2 being the owner of Sigma Electronics Company and Civil Contract while conducting the work, on the incidental spot was so much negligent that he has not taken any precautionary measures to avoid unforeseen events or collusion so as to endanger the human safety.

Due his negligence, the accident was caused and the pillion rider of the C.C. No.
66724/2019 bike succumbed to the occurrence.
Hence accused No.2 is also responsible for the fatal occurrence.
Thereby, the accused No.1 & 2 have committed offences punishable under section 279, 337 & 304(A) IPC & 134(A&B) r/w 187 IMV Act.
3. After receipt of the complaint, the investigating officer registered crime no.147/2019 and visited the spot.
He conducted mahazar in the presence of mahazar witnesses.
Inquired and obtained statement of witnesses.
After completion of an investigation, filed charge sheet against accused No.1 & 2 for the offences p/u/s. 279, 337 & 304(A) IPC & 134(A&B) r/w 187 IMV Act.

4. Accused No.2 being the owner of Sigma Electronics Company and Civil Contract while conducting the work, C.C.
No. 66724/2019 on the incidental spot was so much negligent that he has not taken any precautionary measures to avoid unforeseen events or collusion so as to endanger the human safety.
Due his negligence, the accident was caused and the pillion rider of the bike succumbed to the occurrence.
Hence accused No.2 is also responsible for the fatal occurrence.
Thereby, accused No.1 & 2 have committed an offence punishable under sec. 279 of IPC ?

12. In a road traffic accident, U/s. 279, 337 & 304(A) IPC & 134(A&B) r/w 187 IMV Act, the burden to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 & 2 beyond reasonable doubt lies on the prosecution.
The prosecution shall establish that the accused being rider of the vehicle drove his vehicle in rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life lies on the prosecution.

Further, the burden to prove the guilt of the person who was conducting the work on the certain place was so much negligent that he has not taken any precautionary measures to avoid unforeseen events or collusion so as to endanger the human safety also lies on the prosecution.

In the instant case the prosecution shall establish that accused No.1 was the JCB driver at a particular time and he was working on the incidental spot on that time and turned the bucket of the JCB suddenly when the motorcycle approaches.

Further, the prosecution in respect of accused No.2 shall establish that accused No.2 who was the owner of the Sigma Company and the contractor of the said work where the road was digging in order to lay the electric cables has not taken any precautionary measures is also lies on the prosecution.

sentences.text: In deed, in a criminal case, the burden of proof to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt lies on prosecution.
32. At this juncture, it is pertinent to refer Section 279 & 304(A) IPC.

It reads as follows:
Section 279 of IPC - Rash driving or riding on a public way.
Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
Section 304(A) of IPC - Causing death by negligence.

Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
33. The ingredients of the alleged offences are remained unestablished.

The identification and rashness or negligence of accused has also remained unestablished beyond reasonable C.C. No.
66724/2019 doubt.
It is well settled that when there are two views are possible, the one which favors the accused should be considered.
In other words, the benefit of doubt should go in favor of accused.
In the dearth of evidence, this Court is of considered view that accused is entitled to benefit of doubt.
Accordingly, I answer points No.1 to 4 in the Negative.
34. Point No.5:

For myriad reasons discussed supra, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Accused No.1 & 2 are not found guilty of the alleged offense p/u/s. 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC & 134(A&B) of IMV Act.
Acting U/sec 255(1) of Criminal Procedure Code, accused is hereby acquitted of the offences alleged against them p/u/s. 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC & 134(A&B) of IMV Act.
Bail bond and surety bonds of accused No.1 & 2 stands canceled after completion of appeal period.

On 26.06.2019, at about morning 3:00 am accused No.1 Veerappa, being driver of JBC bearing No. KA-53 N 5264 drove his vehicle, at Mahadevpura Ring Road, Service Road, on the left side of the road, near Kebab Magic Hotel.
He was digging the road to lay electric cables without giving any signal.
He rashly and negligently turned the bucket of the JCB to the right side.
As a result of turning the bucket to the right, JCB dashed to the motorcycle bearing No. KA 04 JU 6918 which was coming from from K.
R. Pura railway station towards Marathalli, i.e., from north to south direction.
Due to the accident, the motorcycle rider and the pillion rider fell down on the road.
The rider Yashwanth.K sustained simple injuries and the pillion rider Ramesh. K.P.
sustained grievous blood injuries on his head, ears and nose and mouth and he succumbed to the occurrence in the Jeevika Hospital.
Accused No.2 being the owner of Sigma Electronics Company and Civil Contract while conducting the work, on the incidental spot was so much negligent that he has not taken any precautionary measures to avoid unforeseen events or collusion so as to endanger the human safety.
Due his negligence, the accident was caused and the pillion rider of the C.C. No.
66724/2019 bike succumbed to the occurrence.
Hence accused No.2 is also responsible for the fatal occurrence.
Thereby, the accused No.1 & 2 have committed offences punishable under section 279, 337 & 304(A) IPC & 134(A&B) r/w 187 IMV Act.

opennyai_summary.issue:
9. The following points arise for my consideration;
Point No.1: Whether prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 26.06.2019, at about 3:00 a.m., at Mahadevpura Ring Road, Service Road, on the left side of the road, near Kebab Magic Hotel, accused no. 1 being the driver of JCB bearing No. No. KA 53 N 5264, he was digging the road to lay electric cables and without giving any signal, he rashly and negligently turned the bucket of the JCB to the right side and dashed to the motorcycle bearing No. KA 04 JU 6918.
Point No.2: Whether prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on aforementioned date,
time and place accused No.1 being the driver of JCB drove his JCB in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle rider, due to the accident, rider and pillon rider of the bike fell down on the road.
Whether prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on aforementioned date,
time and place accused No.1 being the driver of JCB drove his JCB in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle rider, due to the accident, rider and pillon rider of the bike fell down on the road.
Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the aforesaid date, time and place, after causing the accident, accused No.1 & 2 neither informed the incident to the police nor provided any medical assistance to the injured.
Thereby, accused No.1 & 2 have committed an offence p/u/s. 134(A&B) r/w 187 of IMV Act ?
Point No.5: What order?
10.
The prosecution shall establish that the accused being rider of the vehicle drove his vehicle in rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life lies on the prosecution.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
12. In a road traffic accident, U/s. 279, 337 & 304(A) IPC & 134(A&B) r/w 187 IMV Act, the burden to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 & 2 beyond reasonable doubt lies on the prosecution.
Further, the burden to prove the guilt of the person who was conducting the work on the certain place was so much negligent that he has not taken any precautionary measures to avoid unforeseen events or collusion so as to endanger the human safety also lies on the prosecution.
In the instant case the prosecution shall establish that accused No.1 was the JCB driver at a particular time and he was working on the incidental spot on that time and turned the bucket of the JCB suddenly when the motorcycle approaches.
Further, the prosecution in respect of accused No.2 shall establish that accused No.2 who was the owner of the Sigma Company and the contractor of the said work where the road was digging in order to lay the electric cables has not taken any precautionary measures is also lies on the prosecution.
At that time, the driver of JCB suddenly turned JCB towards right side.
The motorcycle damaged and these riders fell down.
The pillion sustained grievous injuries.
All public took the injured to the hospital.
The pillion rider succumbed to the occurrence and rider of the bike sustained small injuries.
Accused No.1 & 2 in response to their 313 Cr.P.C statement though denied that false case was registered, however, they have not put forth their defense.

8 31.
In deed, in a criminal case, the burden of proof to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt lies on prosecution.
The identification and rashness or negligence of accused has also remained unestablished beyond reasonable C.C. No.
66724/2019 doubt.
It is well settled that when there are two views are possible, the one which favors the accused should be considered.
In other words, the benefit of doubt should go in favor of accused.
In the dearth of evidence, this Court is of considered view that accused is entitled to benefit of doubt.
opennyai_summary.decision:
34. Point No.5:
For myriad reasons discussed supra, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Accused No.1 & 2 are not found guilty of the alleged offense p/u/s. 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC & 134(A&B) of IMV Act.
Acting U/sec 255(1) of Criminal Procedure Code, accused is hereby acquitted of the offences alleged against them p/u/s. 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC & 134(A&B) of IMV Act.
Bail bond and surety bonds of accused No.1 & 2 stands canceled after completion of appeal period.
